title: The support-localization triangle of a complex: the construction
statement:
Let $s:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes with complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and fix a finite commutative ring $\Lambda$. Work in the abelian category of all constant-$\Lambda$ module sheaves on the small pro-etale site of $X$, with the underived functors and supported kernel $\mathcal G_Z$ of [def-pur-flasque-support]. Assume that $j$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], so that the canonical comparison $\mathcal G_ZM\xrightarrow{\sim}s_*s^!M$ of [def-pur-flasque-support] is invertible.

For a bounded below cochain complex $K$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], choose the specified K-injective resolution $K\to I(K)$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex], with injective terms, as supplied by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Apply the additive sheaf functors termwise and put
$$
 A(K)=s_*s^!I(K),\qquad B(K)=I(K),\qquad C(K)=j_*j^*I(K).
$$
Let $u:A(K)\to B(K)$ be the inverse of the canonical supported-kernel comparison followed by the kernel inclusion $\mathcal G_ZI(K)\to I(K)$. Let $v:B(K)\to C(K)$ be the open-restriction unit. Thus $vu=0$.

Define the cone complex, with the convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], by
$$
 \operatorname{Cone}(u)^m=B(K)^m\oplus A(K)^{m+1},\qquad
 d(b,a)=(d_Bb+u(a),-d_Aa).
$$
This construction specifies the complexes and maps. It does not identify ordinary restriction $s^{-1}$ with the derived functor $Rs^!$.

split_report.summary: NG: definition-only split, reusing all four existing ingredients and adding the definition of quasi-compactness. STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the imported pro-etale formula silently treats the supported-kernel comparison as invertible without the quasi-compact-complement hypothesis. Make that hypothesis explicit, as in the already repaired def-pur-flasque-support and lem-pur-support-localization-triangle; specify the inclusion through the inverse canonical comparison. Preserve the cone signs and all finite coefficient/site conventions. No new nodes, no proof steps, no Lean changes.
split_report.blueprint: main-20261015 def-pur-support-triangle: first paragraph fixes the closed-open pair and chosen injective resolution; displayed A,B,C are termwise sheaf constructions; final paragraph supplies the kernel inclusion and signed cone. Correct the omitted scope using the supported-sections definition and the intended quasi-compact localization application. This definition has blueprint.is equal to its own id, so from stays null. The related triangle-meaning definition and localization theorem do not state this concrete construction, so same_as remains empty.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NG-422c315a3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Definition-only split with 0 new nodes, no proof steps and no Lean change. The one change adds a hypothesis: the complementary open immersion j must be quasi-compact. That scope was missing from the item, and the report names the change (E7). It is needed because the comparison G_Z M -> s_*s^!M is only supplied for quasi-compact j by the live def-pur-flasque-support. The infinite-product counterexample (lem-pur-infinite-clopen-pair, R = product of F_2, U = union of D(e_n)) shows it can fail otherwise, and the report's argument that injective terms do not avoid the failure is correct (left exactness on 0 -> M -> I^0 -> I^1). The landed Lean module SupportTriangleConstruction already has [QuasiCompact j], finite commutative Lambda, Sheaf(ProEt.topology X)(ModuleCat Lambda) and u = inverse comparison followed by the kernel inclusion, so the new text matches the Lean hypothesis for hypothesis. All three citers already assume j quasi-compact: lem-pur-support-localization-triangle, lem-pur-proetale-support-global-boundary, and def-pur-triangle-meaning (quasi-compactness is stable under its etale base change). In the unit sk-prop-a1-kummer the complement of the zero section is D(t), which is quasi-compact. I read all five stmt_deps. prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist (small-site K-injective resolutions with injective terms) is the right node for the pro-etale site. The cone d(b,a) = (d_B b + u(a), -d_A a) agrees with def-weil-abstract-derived-category and with Mathlib MappingCone.lean:275/288 (summands swapped). I checked that u is a cochain map, vu = 0 and d^2 = 0, and the edge cases Z empty, U empty, K = 0 and Lambda = 0. No SGA source is cited and there are no tool_uses. Maintainer note B10: this node was Lean-closed (reviewed_lean 2026-10-17, reviewed_proof 2026-10-19) and was re-dispatched to stage 1; the split is correct and only brings the text in line with the Lean. The main-20261015 blueprint def-pur-flasque-support and def-pur-support-triangle omit the quasi-compactness hypothesis; record this source error in HUMAN.md.

lean.note: §1(B): The recorded Etale.supportLocalizationTriangle is on the small etale site and does not give the pro-etale cone required here. This module reuses finiteClosedUpperShriek and supportedSectionsComplex, supplies the canonical inverse-supported-unit inclusion, its explicit mapping cone, the specified quotient map, and the triangle with boundary the inverse quotient followed by the negative shifted projection. Its argument I is the chosen injective resolution of the definition; the formula is also defined for any complex, and the item supplies the invertibility proof for injective models.
